"executive_summary": "This paper concludes a series of re-examinations of Raman/Infrared (IR) spectra of representative zincblende semiconductor alloys, namely In1−xGaxAs (1-bond→1-mode), In1−xGaxP (modified 2-mode) and ZnTe1−xSex (traditionally classified as 2-bond→1-mode). The authors challenge the traditional virtual crystal approximation (VCA) description, which treats substitutional disorder at the macroscopic scale and predicts no singularity in physical properties as a function of composition x. Instead, they argue that the bond force constant K, probed via the transverse optical (TO) phonon frequency, is sensitive to local bond distortion and requires a mesoscopic, percolation-based description. They demonstrate that ZnTe1−xSex obeys the same 1-bond→2-mode percolation behaviour as InGaAs and InGaP, thereby unifying the three classes under a single universal percolation paradigm. The study supports a three-oscillator [1 Zn-Te, 2 Zn-Se] version of the percolation model, backed by extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) data and home-made ab initio phonon calculations. The resulting TO and LO Raman lineshapes show good agreement with experimental data, and the TO density of states from density functional theory (DFT) calculations confirms three equidistant oscillators spaced by ~10 cm−1. The authors conclude that even ideally-disordered semiconductor alloys cannot escape a percolation-based description of their basic physical properties, and that vibrational spectroscopies provide natural, non-destructive insight into alloy disorder at the mesoscopic scale. The paper proposes a self-consistent percolation model that can be applied to any zincblende alloy, and highlights the importance of focusing on TO modes rather than LO modes, which suffer from strong electric field coupling that obscures the underlying percolation behaviour. The work has implications for the study of long-scale (self-)organization in alloys, including local ordering and anti-clustering. The study is grounded in existing literature data for ZnTeSe, supplemented by ab initio calculations using the Siesta code within the local density approximation (LDA), and validated against experimental (ωimp, ∆) values for random InGaAs, InGaP and ZnTeSe, as well as (Zn,Be)-chalcogenides, which agree within ~5%. The authors acknowledge support from the IFCPAR and CINES, and note that the LDA overbinding introduces a slight blue-shift of ~20 cm−1 in the TO density of states relative to the Raman lineshape. The paper does not report any new experimental data collection, and the ab initio calculations are performed using standard protocols with 64-atom supercells. The study is primarily theoretical and computational, with the main novelty being the unification of the phonon mode behaviour of different alloy classes under a single percolation framework. The authors emphasize that the percolation scheme is universal and not contingent upon the specific (Ga,In)-substituting species, and that the same behaviour applies to ZnTeSe, which was previously classified as a type (ii) system. The work also highlights the limitations of the MREI-VCA and Elliott-CPA classifications, which fail to account for the observed anomalies in the TO-Raman/IR data of these alloys.
